newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian CERA bank to buy Banque Indosuez Belgique.
newsitem.headline: Belgian CERA bank to buy Banque Indosuez Belgique.

text.p: CERA Bank, Belgium's sixth-largest bank, said on Friday it had struck a basic deal with French Banque Indosuez to buy 80 percent of Banque Indosuez Belgique.
Indosuez Belgique, 99.8 percent owned by its French namesake, is mainly involved on the financial markets and with small and medium-sized enterprises. It has a large trading room in Brussels.
CERA is a bank which focusses on the agricultural sector.
The remainder stays in the hands on Banque Indosuez apart from the 0.2 percent not held by the French bank which stays in public hands.
Banque Indosuez Belgique will become the investment arm of the CERA group but maintains its autonomy. It will continue to get operational support from its French former parent.
CERA said it did not expect the agreement to be finalised before Spring next year after approval by authorities and due diligence procedures.
No financial details of the agreement were immediately available.
French Compagnie de Suez has sold 51 percent of Banque Indosuez to French bank Credit Agricole and is due to sell it a further 29 percent in July 1997.
At the end of June 1996 CERA had total assets of 1,241 billion Belgian francs. It had a 1995 consolidated net profit of 3.376 billion francs.
Indosuez Belgique had assets worth 225 billion francs at the end of 1995 and earned a 418 million franc net profit.
